title: Residential Painting in Archer, FL | Farmhouses & Ranches
description: Residential painting in Archer, FL for farmhouses and ranch homes in Holly Hills, Archer Estates, and beyond. Inside and out, own crews, written warranty.
h1: Residential Painting in Archer, FL for Farmhouses and Ranch Homes
heroIntro: Home painting in Archer means tall farmhouse walls, long ranch rooflines, and interiors that see real use. We repaint both sides of the wall with the same crew and one schedule.

questions: How long does it take to repaint a house in Archer, FL?
Can you paint the inside and outside of my Archer home together?
Do I need to move out while my house is painted?

sections.h2: Two kinds of Archer homes, two sets of problems
body: Most of the homes we repaint around Archer fall into two families. Farmhouses tend to be taller, with wood or fiber-cement lap siding, gables, wraparound or front porches, and a lot of trim. Their weak points are high: gable vents, the top courses of siding, and fascia boards where gutters overflow. Ranch homes, common in Holly Hills and Archer Estates, are lower and wider, with long eave lines, garage doors, and big expanses of wall that face the afternoon sun.

A good residential repaint treats those differently. On a farmhouse we budget more ladder and lift time and more carpentry checks up high. On a ranch we focus on the long sun-baked elevations, the soffits, and the garage and entry doors that get handled every day.

sections.h2: Outside: the shell that keeps weather out
body: The exterior side of a home repaint starts with washing and mildew treatment, then scraping loose paint back to a sound edge, sanding gloss, setting nail pops, and replacing rotted fascia or trim. Every moving joint is re-caulked with a flexible sealant, and bare wood is spot-primed. Then two coats of 100% acrylic go on siding and trim. Details on the full exterior system are on our Archer exterior painting page.

sections.h2: Inside: rooms you keep living in
body: You do not have to leave while we work. Crews move and protect furniture, finish one room before opening the next, and keep the rest of the house usable. A single room usually takes one day; a whole-home interior runs three days to two weeks depending on size and repairs. Washable satin goes where hands and boots hit, flatter sheens where light rakes across walls. Mudrooms and back entries, which see the most traffic on rural properties, get the toughest finish in the house.
Doors, trim, and railings can be upgraded to waterborne urethane enamel, which cures harder than standard wall paint.
Ceilings deserve a mention in older farmhouses, where stains from old roof leaks or textured finishes are common. Our ceiling painting and popcorn removal service can be added to the same scope.

Exterior work is best from October through May. In summer we start early and watch dew point and radar; interiors fill the afternoons. Many homeowners pair an exterior in the cool months with interior rooms whenever it suits them. If the scope includes a new palette, our Archer color consultation can come first. For a sense of how long a fresh exterior should last, read how long exterior paint lasts in Florida.

faqs.q: How long does an exterior repaint take on an Archer farmhouse?
faqs.a: A full exterior usually takes three to seven working days plus washing and dry time. Taller farmhouses with extensive trim sit toward the longer end because of the access work.

faqs.q: Can you do the interior and exterior of my Archer home together?
faqs.a: Yes. One estimate covers both, and we schedule them so the outside goes during good weather while inside rooms fill rain days or hot afternoons.

faqs.q: What warranty comes with a home repaint?
faqs.a: Exterior projects carry a written workmanship warranty of up to 10 years, on top of the manufacturer's product warranty. You also keep labelled touch-up paint for each color.

faqs.q: Do you replace rotted wood before painting?
faqs.a: Yes. Rot and fascia replacement is part of prep, and it is listed on the estimate so you know what is being repaired before any paint goes on.
